notes.meaning: Judah's family line is listed again to introduce important clans and leaders. Only Perez was Judah's actual son, while the others were grandsons or later descendants who headed major family branches. The writer names them here to prepare readers for the detailed lists that follow, especially the family of Shobal.

Shobal's family continues through his son Reaiah and his grandson Jahath down to Ahumai and Lahad. These men were the ancestors of the families who settled in the town of Zorah. God preserved these family records so that his people would remember their heritage in the land.

These verses name the sons of Etam and link them to Hur, whose family founded Bethlehem. In the ancient world, calling a man the father of a city often meant he founded it, governed it, or led its settlers. Hazzelelponi is specially named as their sister, showing she was a respected woman in the tribe's memory.

Ashhur was the leader who founded the town of Tekoa, and he had children through his two wives, Helah and Naarah. His sons became the heads of several distinct family groups in southern Judah. These records show how ordinary households grew into whole communities under God's care.

Koz was the forefather of several other families in Judah, including Anub, Zobebah, and the clans tied to Aharhel. Very little is known today about these men and their towns. Even so, the biblical record includes them to show that every family had a recognized place in Israel.

Jabez is singled out from the long list of names for his honorable character and deep piety. His mother gave him a name that sounded like the Hebrew word for pain because of her hard labor in giving birth to him. Even though his name was linked to sorrow, he lived a faithful and respected life.

Jabez cried out to the God of Israel for true blessing, larger territory, guidance, and protection from evil and sorrow. His prayer asked God to keep him safe so that the pain in his name would not overcome him. God heard his humble request and granted what he asked.

This brief record traces another family line through Chelub and Eshton to the founders of local settlements. Tehinnah was known as the leader or founder of Ir-nahash, which means city of Nahash. These sons and their families lived together as the men of Recah.

Kenaz was the ancestor of Othniel, who became Israel's first judge and leader after the time of Joshua. His brother Seraiah was the father of Joab, who led the valley known as Ge-harashim. This valley earned its name because its inhabitants were skilled workers who practiced craft trades like carpentry and metalwork.

Caleb the son of Jephunneh was the courageous spy who trusted God to give Israel the land of Canaan. His sons and grandsons are listed here among the clans of Judah. Jehallelel and his four sons are also named, representing related families settled in the southern territory.

Mered had children by two different wives, an Egyptian woman named Bithiah and an unnamed Judean woman. Bithiah is called a daughter of Pharaoh, showing that people from Egypt were brought into the community of Judah. His Judean wife bore sons who became leaders and founders of key towns like Gedor, Soco, and Zanoah.

These verses list more Judean families, including the founders of the towns of Keilah and Eshtemoa. Keilah later became famous as the town David rescued from Philistine raiders. The sons of Shimon and Ishi represent other family branches that God preserved in Israel's historical record.

The chapter shifts from the line of Perez to list the descendants of Judah's third son, Shelah. His descendants formed specialized groups of linen workers and leaders who once ruled in the land of Moab. The author notes that these details came from ancient historical records of Israel's earlier days.
